sections.name: File setup, IncidentRow
sections.title: Imports and the incident row type
sections.what: Brings in the display rights check and the repository, and defines the shape of one incident row as the repository returns it. Users do not see this directly.
sections.why: Keeps the row shape tied to whatever the repository returns, so the two stay in step.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a field in the repository's select list breaks the types here.

sections.name: asOf, CricketState
sections.title: Keeps only the latest version of each incident
sections.what: Removes every incident that a later correction has replaced, and defines the summary type that cricket totals use. Users see corrected records replace older ones without duplicates.
sections.why: Corrections are stored as new rows that point to the old one, so this step hides the old row.
sections.watch_out: It only works on the rows it is given; if a correcting row is filtered out first, the old row comes back.

sections.name: foldCricket
sections.title: Adds up the cricket score from balls
sections.what: Walks through the incidents and totals runs (including extras), legal balls and wickets from ball records. It also records the latest time seen and the list of sources.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its comment, which gives the cricket counting rules.
sections.watch_out: Wides and no-balls add runs but not legal balls, so changing the extra-type check changes the over count.

sections.name: getStateAt
sections.title: Gets the match state at a moment
sections.what: The public entry point: fetches an event's incidents as known at the cutoff, drops sources the app may not display, removes replaced records, and totals the rest.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its comment; it bundles the steps so every caller follows the same rules.
sections.watch_out: The rights filter runs before the replaced-record cleanup, so the order can keep an outdated record.

summary: Works out the state of a cricket match at a chosen moment, using only information that was recorded by a chosen cutoff time and that the app is allowed to show.
purpose: Answers the question of what the score, wickets and balls were at a given time, as known by a given cutoff. Other parts of the app call getStateAt; the callers are not listed in this file.
why: The file header says it reads bitemporal data (docs/design-docs/bitemporal-store.md), so later corrections and records seen after the cutoff cannot change the answer and results can be reproduced.
how: 1. Fetch incidents observed by the cutoff and effective by the requested time. 2. Keep only sources the app may display. 3. Drop any record that a later correction replaced. 4. Add up legal balls, runs and wickets from ball records. 5. Return the totals with the latest observed time and the list of sources.
inputs: An event id, an effective time, an observed cutoff time, and stored incident rows (source, type, payload and times) from the repository.
outputs: A CricketState: legal balls, runs, wickets, incident count, latest observed time, and source ids.
risks: The display filter runs before corrections are removed, so a correction from a hidden source can leave the replaced record in the totals. Only cricket is handled here. Extras add to runs, while wides and no-balls add runs but not legal balls.
debug: If totals look wrong, check the observed cutoff first, since records recorded after it are ignored by design. Then check the source's display rights in providers/rights. Then check which records are superseded. Reproduce with the same cutoff in a test.
